title: Kernel Choice Orchestrator: seq-len profiling + architecture fingerprinting
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: The runtime currently picks kernels using a static table keyed by model size and a small set of heuristics. This results in suboptimal throughput/latency trade-offs for workloads with wide seq-len variance and on heterogenous accelerator fleets (A100, H100, 80GB, and mixed memory configs).

Goal: Implement a Kernel Choice Orchestrator that combines lightweight per-deployment architecture fingerprinting, live sequence-length distribution profiling, and an online microbenchmarking fallback to recommend (and optionally switch to) the most efficient kernel implementation per request class. The orchestrator should be conservative about changing kernels for live sessions (prefill->decode continuity), provide an offline autotune path for new models, and expose transparency for cost/latency impact in the Console.

Non-goals: This ticket does not replace the full kernel compiler pipeline or add new kernels. It focuses on selection and routing logic, instrumentation, and a minimal safe switch mechanism at prefill/decode boundaries.

Design summary:
- Architecture fingerprint: small immutable descriptor created at model load time (compute capability, memory topology, interconnect hints) used to narrow candidate kernels.
- Seq-len profiling: runtime keeps a lightweight histogram of observed prefill and decode sequence lengths per route (exponential decay window).
- Cost model: offline microbench runs produce latency/throughput profiles for candidate kernels across a small grid (seqlen, batch). A compact interpolation layer serves fast estimates at runtime.
- Decision policy: a configurable policy evaluates (predicted latency, throughput, token-cost, cache-compatibility) and returns a ranked list of kernel candidates. Policy supports conservative thresholds to avoid destabilizing sessions.
- Fallbacks: if a chosen kernel fails microbench or produces decode errors, orchestrator falls back to verified compatible kernel and records diagnostic artifacts.

Implementation milestones:
1) Instrumentation: add seq-len histogram with bounded memory and per-route tagging (PR #1289).
2) Fingerprinting: extend model load path to compute and persist architecture fingerprint (PR #1302).
3) Microbench harness: implement a short-running microbench that can be scheduled on idle capacity to populate the cost model for a model+arch pair (prototype in experiments/, later moved to prod).
4) Decision engine: implement policy evaluator, ranking, and safe-switch checks.
5) Console hooks: surface recommended kernel, expected delta in latency/cost, and audit log for switches.

Edge cases and safety:
- Prefill/Decode continuity: we will only switch kernels between prefill and decode for an ongoing request if the KV cache layout and tokenizer alignment are compatible. If incompatible, switch only on session boundary.
- Multi-tenant GPU pools: microbench runs must be throttled and run at low priority; results are cached for identical architecture fingerprints.
- Telemetry: all decisions produce an event with input features and selected candidate for offline analysis and regression detection.

Outcomes measured: latency P95 for short-seq (<64) and long-seq (>512) workloads, tokens/sec, and percent requests where orchestrator recommends a non-default kernel.

acceptance_criteria: Seq-len histogram implemented per-route with <1% CPU overhead in canary tests
Model architecture fingerprint persisted and used to narrow candidate kernels
Microbench produces stable latency/throughput profiles for at least 5 representative kernels
Decision engine exposes ranked candidate list and safe-switch logic enforces KV compatibility
Console displays recommended kernel and delta estimates for a selected route
E2E canary on dedicated pool shows >=5% latency improvement for at least two real customer routes with mixed seq-len

comments: 2026-03-03 | Priya Rao: Reviewed architecture fingerprint proposal. Suggested adding interconnect topology (NVLink/PCIe) as a feature for memory-bound kernels. Marked as action item for prototype.
2026-03-05 | Miguel Alvarez: Implemented seq-len histogram prototype. Initial perf measurements show ~0.6% CPU overhead on p3-like nodes. Pushed PR #1289 for review.

2026-03-06 | Performance Team (internal): Microbench harness should include a warmup for caching effects. Otherwise latency estimates for small seqlen are noisy. Recommended 3 warmup runs + median of 5 measured runs.

2026-03-08 | Security (Liaison): Microbench jobs that run on customer-dedicated pools must not leak model weights. Confirmed microbench will use a synthetic graph that exercises kernels but not customer tokens.
2026-03-09 | UX (Jordan Li): Console mock shows how recommendations will surface. Request to include confidence band and link to logs for every recommended switch.
